property_summary: After any sequence of calls, pastBlockTime should always be strictly less than block.timestamp when enough time passes.
After any call to the fallback with value exactly 10 ether, the address(this).balance must be exactly the original balance minus 10 ether when block.number % 15 != 0.

After any successful fallback call with exactly 10 ether, pastBlockTime is always set to a value equal to block.timestamp + 1 (or strictly greater than block.timestamp in the reference, but equal to block.timestamp in the buggy version).
After each fallback call that does not revert, the stored pastBlockTime must be the previous block.timestamp + 1.
After any call, pastBlockTime increases over time (or at least does not decrease), i.e. the rule block.timestamp > pastBlockTime holds after each fallback call that does not revert.
After any two block-producing calls, pastBlockTime is never in the past relative to when the second call was initiated.
After any call that updates pastBlockTime, the new value is always at least block.timestamp + 1, regardless of whether the if-block condition triggers.
After any call to fallback with exactly 10 ether, pastBlockTime is always incremented by at least 1 from the block timestamp during that call.
After a successful call to fallback with exactly 10 ether, pastBlockTime is always greater than the block timestamp at the end of the call, regardless of whether the if-block condition triggers.
After any call, the difference between pastBlockTime and block.timestamp is at most 1 if block.number % 15 == 0, else pastBlockTime remains unchanged from its previous value.
After any call to the fallback with 10 ether, if block.number % 15 == 0, the contract's balance becomes zero, otherwise it remains unchanged.
After calling fallback with 10 ether, if the call does not revert, the contract's balance either decreases by 10 ether (when block.number % 15 == 0) or stays the same (otherwise).
After any successful fallback call with 10 ether, if block.number % 15 == 0, the contract balance decreases by 10 ether; otherwise it remains unchanged.
For all callers and block numbers, if block.number % 15 == 0, the contract must transfer its full balance to the caller only when msg.value == 10 ether.
The balance of the contract must be zero after the fallback function is called when block.number % 15 == 0.
After any call to the fallback function, the contract's pastBlockTime must be strictly greater than the block timestamp before the call.
When block.number % 15 == 0, the contract's fallback must transfer its full balance only when msg.value is exactly 10 ether.
After any successful fallback call with msg.value equal to 10 ether, the contract's balance can never increase above its initial balance minus the value sent, unless it's a multiple-of-15 block.
After any valid fallback call, the contract's balance is either zero or the caller's balance is reduced by exactly 10 ether.
After two fallback calls with different block timestamps, the balance of the contract changes only if the call's block number is a multiple of 15.
After a fallback call succeeds, the pastBlockTime strictly increases compared to its previous value.
After a fallback call succeeds, if the block timestamp equals the stored pastBlockTime, the call must revert because the timestamp is not strictly greater.
